# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Cameron Delgado**
[Street address]
[City], Idaho [ZIP]

**Date:** [date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Submitted online at my.cigna.com, or by phone at 1-800-244-6224

---

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 1, 2026**
- **Member:** Cameron Delgado
- **Member ID:** W425374190
- **Reference number:** POC-F628C11122-30133
- **Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
- **Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), State of Idaho
- **Governing policy:** *Cigna CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026* — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-315%20Shoul%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf
- **Appeal must be received by:** January 28, 2027

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827). The notice dated August 1, 2026 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure my surgeon, Dr. Reyes (orthopedic surgery), has documented that I need.

I want to be helpful rather than argumentative here. If documentation is missing, I am glad to supply it. But before more time passes, I would ask the reviewer to look again at what is already in my chart, because the records line up point by point with the criteria the plan itself publishes in *Cigna CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026*. Below I have matched each criterion to the specific record that supports it.

---

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Imaging findings.** The policy states:

> "MRI or CT shows EITHER of the following findings:
> ◦ Grade 2 or 3 partial-thickness rotator cuff tear (Ellman classification)
> ◦ full-thickness rotator cuff tear (Cofield classification)"

My MRI of the shoulder on May 31, 2026 showed a **full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm**, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. A full-thickness tear is the second of the two findings the policy accepts, and only one of the two is required.

**2. Physical exam findings.** The policy states:

> "Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings (as compared to the non- involved side):"

The first of those two findings is described as:

> "EITHER of the following findings:
> ▪ functionally-limited range of motion
> ▪ measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature"

My exam documents **range of motion limited by pain**, and functionally I **cannot lift my arm above shoulder height**.

The second finding is:

> "ANY of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs:
> ▪ drop arm test
> ▪ painful arc test
> ▪ Jobe test or empty can test
> ▪ lateral Jobe test
> ▪ external rotation lag sign (dropping sign)
> ▪ external rotation resistance test
> ▪ full can test
> ▪ hug up test
> ▪ internal rotation lag sign"

The policy continues that list:

> "▪ internal resistance rotation test (IRRT)
> ▪ internal rotation resistance test at maximal 90° of abduction and maximal external rotation test (IRRTM)
> ▪ lift-off test
> ▪ bear hug test
> ▪ belly press test (Napoleon)
> ▪ belly-off test
> ▪ Neer impingement test
> ▪ Hawkins-Kennedy impingement test
> ▪ Hornblower test (Patte)
> ▪ Yocum test"

My records state that **provocative testing was positive on the affected side**. So that reviewer can match the finding to a named test on the plan's list, I am asking Dr. Reyes's office to send the exam note itself: [attach Dr. Reyes's office/exam note dated ___, identifying by name the positive orthopedic test(s) performed and the side-to-side comparison findings]. If this note was not part of the original packet, that is the one item I would ask the plan to accept now rather than deny the request over.

**3. Function-limiting pain.** The policy states:

> "Symptoms include function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment)"

I have had **24 months of progressive shoulder pain that is not relieved by rest**. I **cannot lift my arm above shoulder height** and I **cannot sleep on the affected side**. That is a direct loss of shoulder function affecting daily activities.

**4. Non-surgical management.** The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

The policy also sets out an exception, and a limit on that exception:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required for an individual who suffers a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear without evidence of a pre-existing chronic rotator cuff tear."

> "Note: The presence of fatty infiltration and/or muscle atrophy on MRI or CT is considered evidence of a pre-existing chronic rotator cuff tear."

> "Therefore, when fatty infiltration and/or muscle atrophy is also present on MRI or CT, three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is required, regardless of whether a discrete traumatic event occurred."

I am not relying on the exception above. My MRI showed grade 2 fatty atrophy, and my records document the following course of non-surgical care:

- **NSAIDs for 4 months**, with inadequate relief;
- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, **18 visits from May 3, 2026 through July 12, 2026 (10 weeks)**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- **Corticosteroid injection on June 9, 2026**, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.

This is provider-directed care, it spans more than three months, and it failed to relieve my symptoms.

**5. Other conditions excluded.** The policy states:

> "Other potential pathological conditions have been excluded, including, but not limited to the following: fracture, thoracic outlet syndrome, brachial plexus disorders, referred neck pain, cervical radiculopathy, and advanced glenohumeral osteoarthritis."

[Ask Dr. Reyes's office to provide the chart documentation addressing the exclusion of these other conditions, if it was not included in the original submission.]

---

## One request about the criteria themselves

The excerpts of *CMM-315* I have been able to obtain include a criterion that ends in a colon and introduces additional requirements that were not reproduced in the material available to me. The policy therefore lists further conditions I cannot see. **If the plan applied a criterion I have not addressed above, I ask that the appeal response identify it specifically**, along with the exact document or finding the plan considers missing. A denial for incomplete documentation is difficult for me to cure unless I am told which item is absent.

I would also note that the denial notice does not name the specific records the reviewer found lacking. I have not quoted the notice here because it states a conclusion rather than a criterion; my aim is to address the plan's published criteria directly.

---

## What I am asking Cigna to do

1. Reconsider and overturn the denial of CPT 29827 and approve the rotator cuff repair recommended by Dr. Reyes.
2. If any document is still needed, tell me in writing exactly which one, and allow me a reasonable opportunity to submit it before the request is denied again.
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic surgery.
4. Send me a copy of the full clinical criteria that were applied to my request.

I have attached, or am arranging to have my surgeon's office send, the following: the MRI report of May 31, 2026; the physical therapy discharge note covering May 3 – July 12, 2026; the injection and medication records; and Dr. Reyes's office notes, including the physical exam findings. [List any additional enclosures here.]

My surgeon has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and the records in my chart track the plan's own criteria. I would be grateful for a careful second look. Please contact me at [phone] or [email] if anything further is needed.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Delgado**
Member ID: W425374190
Reference number: POC-F628C11122-30133
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [list enclosed documents]
**cc:** [Reyes, MD — orthopedic surgery, if you wish to copy your surgeon]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
